bullets.title: MASSIVE AI-driven tech selloff: S&P -2%, NDX -4.6% WoW; semis worst in decades
bullets.body: The week's dominant story was a historic momentum unwind in AI/tech. The NDX fell -4.24% WoW vs SPX -1.95%, the widest NDX/SPX realized vol spread in two decades (~18 vol points). Mag 7 shed >$1T in market cap (NVDA -8.6%, GOOGL -8.3%), with the Mag 7 basket underperforming SPX by 9% MTD. Levered ETF rebalancing alone generated an estimated $42bn of equity supply on Tuesday; short gamma reached historical highs at -$16bn/1% move. GS Prime reported the largest Info Tech + Comm Svcs combined net selling in over 10 years. The selloff was mechanical and positioning-driven: hedge funds net sold US equities at the fastest pace since Liberation Day, with AI Tech Beneficiaries seeing the largest weekly selling since the trade began (~3.4 z-score event). Retail aggressively bought the dip (~$43bn Monday–Thursday, 100th percentile).

bullets.title: Semis/memory supercycle intact but crowded; SOX down 5.3% on leverage unwind
bullets.body: Despite the selloff, fundamentals remained strong. MU delivered a historic beat: Q3 revenue $41.46B (+15.5% vs consensus), gross margin 84.9%, EPS $25.11 (+20%), and Q4 guide of $50B revenue and $31 EPS—both ~20% above Street. MU disclosed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements covering ~20% DRAM and ~33% NAND volume through 2030, representing ~$100B minimum committed revenue at floor prices described as 'well above prior cycle peak margins.' Supply tightness expected beyond 2027, with demand substantially exceeding supply into 2028. HBM TAM pulled forward to >$100B in 2027. Semis positioning at +3z on 6-month z-scores; prior breaks above +2.5z marked pauses or reversals. Tech Hardware positioning even more extreme at >4z.

bullets.title: Fed hawkishness intensifies: BofA/Deutsche see hikes; Fed likely on hold until 2H27 per JPM
bullets.body: The macro debate shifted decisively hawkish. BofA now forecasts 75bp of Fed rate hikes this year; Deutsche Bank 50bp. Nine FOMC members anticipate hikes, six looking for two or more. Core PCE for May printed 0.32% m/m (in line), but core services ex-housing reaccelerated to 0.50% MoM—a full percentage point above pre-COVID pace. JPMorgan's EM team expects Fed on hold until 2H27, arguing oil disinflation offsets prior inflation concerns. 22V Research puts the modal scenario at 2-3 credibility hikes in late 2026/early 2027. Morgan Stanley needs core PCE at ≤0.2% m/m to stay on hold; 0.3%+ could prompt hike thinking. Fed Chair Warsh signaled focus on price stability and reduced forward guidance, raising rate vol. Markets priced ~33–40bp of hikes through year-end.

bullets.title: Oil collapses 8-9% on Strait of Hormuz reopening; Brent near pre-war levels
bullets.body: WTI crude fell ~8.7% on the week—its 9th consecutive losing session—as Persian Gulf crude exports recovered to 75% of pre-war levels and Saudi Aramco resumed loadings at Ras Tanura. Brent fell below pre-conflict levels. JPMorgan revised its 2026 Brent forecast to $86 (Q3), $80 (Q4), $78 (YE), and $64 in 2027. The oil drop is driving headline disinflation globally and improving EM current accounts, but core services inflation remains sticky. Refiners (PBF, DK, VLO) surged 8-13% on margin relief; oil services lagged.

bullets.title: Russell recon at record $244B notional; Communication Services gets $11.7B inflows
bullets.body: The 2026 Russell reconstitution effective June 26 was the largest in history at ~$244B notional turnover (2021 record: $151B). NVDA Russell 1000 Growth upweight surged from $1.96B to $4.23B. AAPL, AMZN, MSFT shifted from Growth to Value and were the largest net sell names. GOOGL, MU, AMD, and CAT saw sizeable Value-to-Growth shifts. Communication Services sector received $11.7B in passive inflows; Consumer Discretionary saw $9.5B outflows. Russell 2000 turnover more than doubled to ~$77B gross notional.

bullets.title: AAPL raises Mac/iPad prices 15-25% on memory cost surge; iPhone prices deferred
bullets.body: Apple announced 15-25% price increases on MacBooks, iPads, HomePods, and other hardware, citing DRAM/NAND cost pressures from data center demand. iPhone prices were not raised immediately; September iPhone 18 launch expected to carry $100+ increases. AAPL fell ~6% on the announcement—worst day since April 2025. Price elasticity concerns are real: JPM noted the magnitude suggests prior mid-single-digit iPhone increase expectations were too optimistic. Bears worry about demand destruction; bulls cite installment-plan inelasticity and margin defense.

bullets.title: Sector rotation: defensives, small caps, cyclicals lead; AI momentum unwind accelerates
bullets.body: While tech imploded, the rotation was orderly. Russell 2000 +1.02% WoW vs Nasdaq -4.6%. Healthcare +6%, Staples +3%, Utilities +4.5%, REITs +4% were the best performing sectors. Finance sector led 52-week highs. Piper, Wolfe, and others noted a 'mega rotation' from mega-cap tech into cyclicals and value—described as a stock-picker's market. All 32 large banks passed DFAST stress tests with CET1 at 11.2% stressed minimum; JPM, WFC, MS, BNY raised dividends. Regional banks (FITB +7.3%, PNC +5.6%) outperformed.

bullets.title: OpenAI IPO delayed to 2027; GPT-5.6 release staggered by Trump admin
bullets.body: OpenAI is leaning toward delaying its IPO until 2027, citing inability to achieve the $1T valuation target and post-SPCX retail investor apathy. The Trump administration separately requested OpenAI stagger the GPT-5.6 rollout to 20 government-approved partners over national security concerns. The White House also restricted Anthropic's Mythos 5 and Fable 5 for foreign access. Chinese LLM alternatives (Z.ai GLM-5.2) gained traction during the period of US frontier model restriction. Goldman estimates AI market gains now require more optimistic adoption assumptions to be justified.

bullets.title: FCF 'value transfer' from hyperscalers to memory is the key AI bear case this week
bullets.body: The dominant bearish narrative for AI tech was that Micron's $100B+ strategic customer agreements—with floor prices 'well above prior peak margins'—represent a massive FCF transfer from hyperscalers (MSFT, AMZN, META, GOOGL, ORCL) to memory suppliers. MSFT is raising Xbox prices 23% and Apple is raising Mac prices 15-25%, both citing memory cost inflation. AMZN raised GPU instance prices +20% July 1 across Blackwell/Hopper/Ampere. Samsung and SK Hynix are planning $648B and $29.4B investment programs respectively, adding to supply eventually but confirming structural demand.

bullets.title: May PCE in line; 2Q GDP trimmed to 2.1% on weak trade; May trade deficit widened to -$105.7B
bullets.body: May core PCE printed 0.32% m/m (below 0.36% hawkish expectations), 3.4% y/y. Personal income +0.68% m/m; real spending +0.3%. The savings rate held flat at 3.0%. May trade deficit widened sharply to -$105.7B as exports fell 6.6% m/m (broad-based weakness) while imports firmed. Real capital goods imports fell 1.4% m/m—first decline of the year. Net trade drag reduced 2Q GDP tracking to 2.1% from 2.5% (Morgan Stanley). Underlying domestic demand remained more resilient at 2.4%. Manufacturing PMI hit a 4-year high in June (55.7), while services PMI weakened.

bullets.title: Citi downgrades Tech and Semis to Market Weight; upgrades Software
bullets.body: Citi's US Equity Strategy cut Information Technology, Semiconductors, and Hardware from Overweight to Market Weight, citing stretched valuations despite strong fundamentals. Software was simultaneously upgraded to Market Weight from Underweight. The note cited four headwinds on mega-cap tech: funding concerns, company-specific issues (AAPL margins, MSFT Azure limits, AMZN consumer, GOOGL capex, AVGO/NVDA competition), and technicals breaking 200-DMA. Separately, Citi raised MU PT to $1,400 (10x CY27 EPS) and SNDK PT to $2,500 on tight supply through CY27+.

bullets.title: JPMorgan raises S&P 500 YE target to 7,800; raises 2026 EPS to $350 (+29% YoY)
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Dubravko raised the S&P 500 year-end 2026 price target from 7,600 to 7,800 (+5.9% upside), driven by ~10% consensus EPS upgrades to $350 for 2026 and $390 for 2027. JPM raised its mid-year Global Equity target and maintained a Tactically Bullish call, noting the 'everything rally' should fade into concentrated AI leadership. Barclays and Stifel also raised targets to 7,800. Tom Lee raised his YE target to 8,000 from 7,700. JPM favors Tech, AI Upstream, Banks, and Defense overweight.

bullets.title: Global AI capex hitting $800B in 2026; power bottleneck and grid capacity are binding constraints
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's macro forum estimated AI capex at ~$800B in 2026 and ~$1.1T in 2027. Five hyperscalers committed $730B in 2026 capex (+77% y/y), doubling cumulative ChatGPT-era spend. Global M&A activity hit record $1.89T (past 4Q) with 49% stock-financed (highest since 2001). US datacenter headroom approaching zero by 2027; behind-the-meter power is becoming the marginal solution. Virginia approved $0.011/kWh electricity tax on data centers effective July 2026. JPM's capex nowcaster showed global investment goods spending at 10.2% annualized for 2Q26, up from 6.8% in 1Q.

bullets.title: Leveraged ETF short gamma at all-time highs; month/quarter-end rebalancing adds to supply
bullets.body: Levered ETF AUM reached ~$200B with $400B in net exposure; trading volumes 50% above H1 2025 pace. Short gamma reached -$16B/1% SPX move with 3/4 of exposure benchmarked to Semis, NDX, or Tech single names. A -2% one-day SPX selloff would create ~$30B of additional supply from macro systematic strategies over the following week. Goldman estimated $30B of US equity selling into month/quarter-end (89th percentile); JPMorgan estimated ~$165B equity selling/bond buying. Pension funds at 110% funding (highest since 2001) are mechanically de-risking.

bullets.title: GOOGL loses multiple DeepMind researchers to Anthropic/OpenAI; Gemini 3.5 Pro delayed
bullets.body: Google suffered high-profile AI talent departures throughout the week: John Jumper (AlphaFold co-creator, 2024 Nobel laureate) joined Anthropic; Noam Shazeer (Gemini co-lead) joined OpenAI; Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel also departed to Anthropic. Gemini 3.5 Pro was delayed from June to July for additional real-world testing. GOOGL fell ~5-8% across the week on these combined concerns. DeepMind CEO Hassabis publicly downplayed the departures. Anthropic simultaneously accused Alibaba of using 25K fraudulent accounts to conduct large-scale distillation attacks on its Claude models.

bullets.title: ECB and BoE signal further rate hikes despite lower energy prices; ECB September hike likely
bullets.body: ECB's Lagarde and Schnabel both signaled another rate hike remains 'firmly on the table.' Schnabel stated 'from today's perspective, we will need to raise interest rates further.' JPMorgan still forecasts a final ECB hike in September despite falling energy prices, as core inflation remains above target-consistent levels and growth has proven resilient. Eurozone composite PMI improved 0.9pt to 49.5 in June, with 2Q GDP forecast raised to 0.5% q/q saar. ECB consumer inflation expectations fell 0.5pp to 3.5% in May but remain above pre-conflict levels. UK June PMI fell to 49.4; BoE hike call maintained.

bullets.title: AWS-3 spectrum reauction concludes at $3.6B; Verizon wins 82 licenses for $3.2B
bullets.body: FCC Auction 113 (AWS-3 reauction) concluded with $3.56B total proceeds, slightly above the original 2015 auction value. Verizon purchased 82 licenses in major markets for $3.2B, the largest winner. T-Mobile won 102 licenses. National MNOs collectively won 194/200 licenses representing >99.5% of proceeds. AT&T separately won $120.8M in net payments. The result is viewed as spectrum-positive for the wireless ecosystem ahead of the upper C-Band auction which must complete before July 2027.

bullets.title: South Korea KOSPI crashed 10% on leveraged ETF concerns; 5th largest decline in market history
bullets.body: Korea's KOSPI fell nearly 10% on Tuesday—its 5th largest daily percentage decline in market history—driven by regulatory concerns about leveraged chip-linked ETFs and amplified by margin loan unwinds (retail had added $80B YTD). Circuit breakers were triggered for 20 minutes. Samsung and SK Hynix each fell >12%. Korean regulator admitted leveraged single-stock ETF approvals were 'prepared hastily.' Foreign investors sold $2.5B Korean equities overnight. The selloff spread to US memory/semis and contributed to the week's broader tech derisking, with $6B in Korean chip ETF outflows in a single day.

bullets.title: Crimea deteriorating rapidly; Ukraine strikes degrade Russian logistics and air defenses
bullets.body: Geopolitical intelligence highlighted accelerating Ukrainian strikes on Crimea's military infrastructure causing 'materially greater damage than consensus expected.' Russian authorities declared a full state of emergency for Crimea due to acute fuel, power, and supply shortages. Thousands of vehicles queued to leave via the Kerch Bridge; summer tourism will fail. Ukrainian forces destroyed material parts of Russian air defenses and now have relatively unhindered access to key targets. Rapid Crimea deterioration could force Putin toward escalation rather than negotiations.
